  6384: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL bool c_ir_wide_atomic_runtime_required(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, IrTypeId atomic_type)
  6385: {
  6386:     IrType* type = ir_type_from_id(&builder->program->types, atomic_type);
  6387:     return type && type->is_atomic && type->layout.resolved && type->layout.size == 16 &&
  6388:            builder->target.cpu_arch == CPU_ARCH_X86_64 &&
  6389:            !target_cpu_feature_has(builder->target, TARGET_CPU_FEATURE_X86_CX16);
  6390: }
  6391: 
  6392: // The type-specific libatomic entry points erase the C object's signedness,
  6393: // atomic/volatile qualifiers and aggregate spelling at their ABI boundary.
  6394: // Use one unsigned bit representation and one plain pointer type so every
  6395: // source spelling in a translation unit reuses exactly one imported symbol.
  6396: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL bool c_ir_wide_atomic_runtime_arguments(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, IrValueId place, IrTypeId atomic_type,
  6397:                                                            IrSourceRange source, IrTypeId* bits_type_out, IrTypeId* pointer_type_out,
  6398:                                                            IrValueId* address_out)
  6399: {
  6400:     IrTypeId bits_type = c_ir_builder_scalar_type(builder, C_TYPE_UNSIGNED_INT128);
  6401:     IrValueId bits_place = bits_type.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID
  6402:                                ? c_ir_atomic_aggregate_bits_place(builder, place, atomic_type, bits_type, source)
  6403:                                : IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
  6404:     IrTypeId bits_place_type = bits_place.value < builder->function->value_count
  6405:                                    ? builder->function->values[bits_place.value].canonical_type
  6406:                                    : IR_TYPE_ID_INVALID;
  6407:     IrValueId qualified_address = bits_place_type.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID
  6408:                                       ? c_ir_emit_address_of_place(builder, bits_place, bits_place_type, source)
  6409:                                       : IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
  6410:     IrTypeId pointer_type = bits_type.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID
  6411:                                 ? c_ir_add_pointer_type(builder->program, builder->pointer_types, bits_type)
  6412:                                 : IR_TYPE_ID_INVALID;
  6413:     IrValueId address = qualified_address.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID && pointer_type.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID
  6414:                             ? c_ir_emit_cast_instruction(builder, qualified_address, pointer_type,
  6415:                                                          IR_CONVERSION_POINTER_REINTERPRET, source)
  6416:                             : IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
  6417:     bool valid = bits_place.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID && pointer_type.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID &&
  6418:                  address.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID;
  6419:     if (!valid && !builder->failure_message.length)
  6420:     {
  6421:         builder->failure_message = S8("could not form a canonical address for a 16-byte atomic runtime call");
  6422:     }
  6423:     if (valid)
  6424:     {
  6425:         *bits_type_out = bits_type;
  6426:         *pointer_type_out = pointer_type;
  6427:         *address_out = address;
  6428:     }
  6429:     return valid;
  6430: }

  8792:     {

  8808:                 suffix_valid = false;

  8762:     {
  8763:         result = value <= (((u64)1 << (integer->bit_width - 1)) - 1);
  8764:     }
  8765: 
  8766:     return result;
  8767: }

  8891: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL IrValueId c_ir_emit_integer(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, CToken token)
  8892: {
  8893:     u64 value = 0;
  8894:     if (!c_conditional_number(c_token_spelling(builder->preprocess.spelling_base, token), &value))
  8895:     {
  8896:         return IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
  8897:     }
  8898:     IrTypeId type = c_ir_integer_literal_type(builder, c_token_spelling(builder->preprocess.spelling_base, token), value);

 10403: // One operand in the common real type the usual arithmetic conversions pick.
 10404: // Only an integer operand can lose anything here -- a float widens into a
 10405: // double exactly and every encoded value is already exact in the x87 format --
 10406: // but that loss is real: `16777217 * 1.0f` holds 2^24 because the integer
 10407: // rounds to float before the multiply, not after it.
 10408: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL bool c_ir_ext80_value_convert(CIrExt80Value* value, u8 rank)
 10409: {
 10410:     bool result = true;
 10411:     if (value->rank != rank && rank != C_IR_EXT80_RANK_LONG_DOUBLE && !c_ir_ext80_value_is_special(*value) && value->significand)
 10412:     {
 10413:         CIrExt80Big numerator;
 10414:         CIrExt80Big denominator;
 10415:         s32 binary_exponent = 0;
 10416:         bool negative = false;
 10417:         c_ir_ext80_big_set_u64(&denominator, 1);
 10418:         result = c_ir_ext80_value_rational(*value, &numerator, &binary_exponent, &negative) &&
 10419:                  c_ir_ext80_value_round(&numerator, &denominator, binary_exponent, negative, rank, value);
 10420:     }
 10421:     value->rank = rank;
 10422: 
 10423:     return result;
 10424: }
 10425: 
 10426: // The IEEE special cases, which answer before the rational core sees anything.
 10427: // The invalid combinations among them -- inf minus inf, inf times zero, inf
 10428: // over inf, zero over zero -- have to give the same answer as
 10429: // c_ir_fold_float_invalid_operation gives an in-function constant, because
 10430: // the sign IEEE-754 leaves unspecified is a compatibility choice and the two
 10431: // paths would otherwise print `nan` and `-nan` for one spelling.  They also
 10432: // do not care where the operation would round: the NaN is the same value at
 10433: // every precision and widens exactly.
 10434: //
 10435: // A NaN operand wins outright and keeps its own sign, the left one first; the
 10436: // sign flip a subtraction applies to its right operand happens only after
 10437: // that, which is why `1.0L - -nan` is still negative.  Everything else is the

 10623: // The usual arithmetic conversions decide where an operation rounds: both
 10624: // operands convert to the common real type first and the result rounds there.

 10627: // for it would be silently wrong rather than merely absent.

 10648: // One numeric token as the long double value it converts to.  The three cases
 10649: // are the literal's own type: an L-suffixed spelling is already this format, a
 10650: // plain or f-suffixed spelling rounds to double or float first and widens
 10651: // exactly, and an integer spelling converts from its own integer type, where a
 10652: // leading minus on an unsigned literal wraps before the widening.
 10653: //
 10654: // A spelling whose magnitude does not fit its own type is not a refusal: C
 10655: // gives it the infinity or the signed zero, and musl spells `INFINITY` as
 10656: // `1e5000f` whenever the compiler does not offer the GNU builtins, which is
 10657: // how an overflowing literal reaches a static initializer in the first place.

 25540: /* Resolves the C result type of a sizeof/alignof expression operand strictly: every
 25541:    sub-operand must resolve through a mapped entity, literal, cast, or call before any
 25542:    type is combined, and binary operators apply the usual arithmetic conversions (so
 25543:    narrow operands promote to int and mixed widths take the wider side). Returning
 25544:    false defers to the older per-shape paths and ultimately the caller's fallback; a
 25545:    guessed type must never come out of this function, because the guessed size folds
 25546:    silently into the program (the 2026-08-08 array-bound incident, and the same
 25547:    defect shape in function bodies). */
 25548: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL bool c_ir_sizeof_operand_type_attempt_depth(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, u32 start, u32 end, IrTypeId* type_out, u32 remaining_depth, bool promote_bit_fields)
 25549: {
 25550:     // This resolver is a speculative type query: false lets the caller use
 25551:     // the ordinary expression paths.  Bound its recursive precedence walk so
 25552:     // adversarially deep, otherwise-valid expressions cannot exhaust the host
 25553:     // stack in sanitizer/fuzz configurations, whose instrumented frames are
 25554:     // substantially larger than Release frames.
 25555:     if (!remaining_depth)
 25556:     {
 25557:         return false;
 25558:     }
 25559:     remaining_depth -= 1;
 25560:     // GNU __extension__ is a diagnostic-only marker on the expression that
 25561:     // follows it; it contributes no value and no type of its own, so strip it
 25562:     // the same way a redundant parenthesis is stripped, and keep stripping
 25563:     // both until neither applies.  musl's <complex.h> spells `I` as
 25564:     // `(__extension__ (0.0f+1.0fi))` under __GNUC__, and leaving the marker in
 25565:     // this walk made the whole group resolve as the leading `0.0f` -- so
 25566:     // `0*I` was a float, `2.0+0*I` was a double, and every <tgmath.h> macro
 25567:     // reached through a complex argument selected the real function.
 25568:     bool trimmed = true;
 25569:     while (trimmed)
 25570:     {
 25571:         trimmed = false;
 25572:         while (start < end && c_token_is_punctuator(&builder->preprocess.tokens[start], C_PUNCTUATOR_LEFT_PARENTHESIS) &&
 25573:                c_ir_matching_delimiter_cached(builder, start, end, C_PUNCTUATOR_LEFT_PARENTHESIS, C_PUNCTUATOR_RIGHT_PARENTHESIS) == end - 1)

 25575:             start += 1;
 25576:             end -= 1;
 25577:             trimmed = true;
 25578:         }

 30828: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL IrTypeId c_ir_usual_arithmetic_type(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, IrTypeId left_type, IrTypeId right_type)
 30829: {
 30830:     IrType* left = ir_type_from_id(&builder->program->types, left_type);
 30831:     IrType* right = ir_type_from_id(&builder->program->types, right_type);
 30832:     if (!left || !right)
 30833:     {
 30834:         return IR_TYPE_ID_INVALID;
 30835:     }
 30836:     // One complex operand makes the result complex, over the usual arithmetic
 30837:     // type of the two corresponding real types (C11 6.3.1.8p1).
 30838:     if (left->is_complex || right->is_complex)
 30839:     {
 30840:         return c_ir_complex_result_type(builder, left_type, right_type);
 30841:     }
 30842:     if (left->kind == IR_TYPE_BOOLEAN || left->kind == IR_TYPE_ENUM || (left->kind == IR_TYPE_INTEGER && left->bit_width < 32))
 30843:     {
 30844:         left_type = builder->s32_type;
 30845:         left = ir_type_from_id(&builder->program->types, left_type);
 30846:     }
 30847:     if (right->kind == IR_TYPE_BOOLEAN || right->kind == IR_TYPE_ENUM || (right->kind == IR_TYPE_INTEGER && right->bit_width < 32))
 30848:     {
 30849:         right_type = builder->s32_type;
 30850:         right = ir_type_from_id(&builder->program->types, right_type);

 41765: // The evaluator's unary `+`/`-` on an integer constant of `*type`
 41766: // (c_ir_constant_apply_unary): a boolean or narrow operand is promoted to
 41767: // int first -- no literal type is that narrow, but the rule is kept so the
 41768: // arm and the evaluator cannot disagree -- and the result is masked to the
 41769: // operand's width.  False for the 128-bit operand, whose wide negate stays
 41770: // with the evaluator.

 41786: }
